description: Security monitoring and threat response settings

auto_pause_on_high.description: Automatically pause the container when a high-severity threat is detected

auto_kill_on_critical.description: Automatically kill the container when a critical-severity threat is detected

poll_interval_sec.description: How often to collect container stats (seconds)

file_read_threshold_mb.description: Alert when the container reads more than this many MB in a single poll interval

file_read_rate_mb_per_sec.description: Alert when the sustained file read rate exceeds this threshold (MB/s)

audit_log_retention_days.description: Number of days to retain audit log files

process_count_threshold.description: Maximum process count before a fork-bomb alert (0 = disabled)

process_spawn_rate_threshold.description: Maximum processes spawned per poll interval before an alert (0 = disabled)

forensics_on_kill.description: Preserve a forensic COPY of the container (incus copy, capped at 3 per container, oldest pruned) before an auto-kill on a critical threat deletes it — the copy is made while the container still runs and survives the kill (the original still auto-deletes as usual); the kill fires exactly when the container's state is most worth investigating. Best-effort: a failed copy never blocks or delays the response. Opt-in; default: false.

reverse_shell_one_liners.description: Severity for interpreter one-liner reverse-shell matches (python -c, python3 -c, perl -e, ruby -e, php -r): 'critical' (default — auto-kills when auto_kill_on_critical is on), 'warn' (logged and audited, never kills or pauses), or 'off' (not flagged at all). Interpreter one-liners only ever match when the command also carries a real network indicator (a socket/tcp/udp/connect keyword, an IP, or a host:port endpoint). The unambiguous reverse-shell patterns (nc -e, /dev/tcp/, socat EXEC:, an interactive shell, ...) always stay critical regardless of this setting. See issue #842.
